title: Clockwork bridging cadence: handoff & follow-ups (2029-04-10)
content:
Shift window: 2029-04-10 07:30 UTC -> 2029-04-10 19:30 UTC
Owners on deck: Aisha (primary), Daniel (backup), María (bridge), Owen (pager support)
Bridge info: ephemeral bridge created at 07:45 UTC. Link in linear ticket above.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Primary user impact: intermittent 503s and elevated p95 token generation time between 09:10-10:05 UTC and again 14:40-15:55 UTC. Roughly 1.6% of requests failed at peak; overall platform throughput largely unaffected.
- Root cause (initial triage): autoscaler mis-evaluation + aggressive KV-cache reclamation on a subset of dedicated nodes under small-queued-burst pattern.
- Mitigations applied: throttled cache eviction, manual node cordon on pool gpu-dedicated-east-2a, reverted an autoscaler threshold change pushed yesterday (PR #378).

Detailed timeline (notes written live):
- 07:30 shift start: quick roll call, verify dashboards, no elevated alerts. Canary requests normal.
- 09:08 first spike: elevated 500/503 alerts from route /v1/generate (hosted-api). P95 token time jumped from 230ms -> 980ms. Pager notification (ops level 2) fired.
- 09:12 bridged: María opened ephemeral bridge. Started correlation with autoscaler and node metrics.
- 09:17 identified pattern: spike correlated with a sustained burst from a customer test harness routing a higher-than-normal batch size to a dedicated pool. Autoscaler recommended scale-down earlier and then tried to scale up; the window left gap while cache was being rehydrated.
- 09:25 SRE action: increased autoscaler stabilization window, added a temporary scale-up override for gpu-dedicated-east-2a. Also disabled a recent experimental eviction policy (kv-evict-v2) which was reclaiming cached KV aggressively.
- 09:35 error rate decreasing; by 10:05 token p95 back to ~260ms and 503s near zero.
- 12:20 began seeing small error blips on a different shard (gpu-dedicated-west-1b) — likely the same pattern but lower amplitude. Logged to JIRA-SRE-2148.
- 14:40 second larger pulse: 503s + slow tail observed. Investigation found that a rolling config push (PR #382) had changed the autoscaler target for dedicated pools to use CPU headroom metric in addition to queue length; in low queue cases this produced oscillation.
- 14:55 emergency rollback of PR #382 to previous autoscaler logic. Throttled multi-region routing for affected customer test-harness.
- 15:20 normalized, continued watch until 16:30, then handed monitoring to evening shift with watch item.

Actions taken (concrete):
- Immediate: rollback PR #382 (owner: infra-team, PR linked in artifacts), disabled kv-evict-v2 on dedicated pools (owner: serving-runtime; actioned by Daniel).
- Short-term follow-up (owner / ETA):
  - SRE-2148 (assigned to Owen) — run extended soak on dedicated pools with synthetic traffic to reproduce and collect traces (ETA 2029-04-13).
  - INF-432 (Linear) — add a guard in autoscaler to avoid oscillation when queue length < 8 and recent scale events < 5m (ETA 2029-04-12).
  - Runbook update: kv-cache-reclaim runbook needs a new step for partial-recoveries: add a phased eviction rollback and a visibility dashboard for eviction rate (owner: Aisha / draft updated 2029-04-11).

Low-friction improvements to implement (notes to product/infra):
- Add a short-circuit in routing for synthetic heavy test-harness traffic (customer-identifiers flagged) so test traffic can be rate-limited or routed to a non-prod pool.
- Add autoscaler telemetry tag to every scale action so we can correlate decisions to eviction events quickly.
- Hysteresis param suggestion: increase stabilization window default from 30s -> 90s for dedicated gpu pools.

Open items / unresolved at handoff:
- Follow-up trace correlation between kv eviction events and token-generation tail needed (assigned Owen).
- Need a canary job to validate PRs that touch autoscaler logic under bursty synthetic workloads (infra + release-eng).
- Customer outreach: notify affected customer test-harness about temporary throttling and request they shift long-running soak to off-peak (owner: customer-success, point: Priya Sharma).

Runbook drafts / edits made during shift (quick pointers):
- file: confluence://runbooks/kv-cache-reclaim (draft updated): added a quick rollback snippet and command sequence for disabling kv-evict-v2 on a running pool.
- autoscaler runbook: inserted a new troubleshooting section "oscillation checks" with sample queries and recommended metric thresholds.

Post-shift retrospective notes (short):
- Why this slipped through: recent PRs changed two interacting systems (autoscaler + eviction policy) without an integration soak. Need cross-team gating for changes that affect routing/scale decisions.
- What saved us: fast bridge, clear owner handoffs, and the ability to roll back config via Prometheus-flags / feature-gates.
- One surprising find: eviction rate graphs were below the standard alerting threshold; we should consider a "delta-of-eviction-rate" alert to catch sudden ramps even if absolute is low.

Notes to next shift (explicit):
- Watch eviction-rate (metric: serving.kv.eviction.rate) for any upticks > 3x baseline in a 5m window.
- Monitor autoscaler decision log (tag: autoscaler.decision) for repeated scale-down/up within 10m.
- Validation: run smoke generate calls to /v1/generate on dedicated pools every 15m for 2h after any config change.
- Handoff ticket: JIRA-SRE-2148 — summary + traces attached; please add any new findings to the ticket and @mention Aisha.

Quick checklist (for next oncall):
- [ ] Confirm PR #382 remains rolled back in infra repo and note any revert-bundles.
- [ ] Verify synthetic-harness is rate-limited / flagged in routing.
- [ ] Follow the trace correlation task (Owen) and update SRE-2148 with results.
- [ ] If eviction-rate delta alert shows, escalate to serving-runtime and infra on-call.

Random notes / personal:
- Remember to schedule a 30m sync with release-eng to propose a pre-merge soak gate for autoscaler changes.
- Maria spotted a small dashboard typo (eviction/day) — I corrected it at 16:02 but could use a second eyeball.

End of log. Handoff: 2029-04-10 19:30 UTC to evening oncall (lead: Kenji Tanaka).
